citation: Li Wenzi, Zhu Hua, Wen Li, et al. Application Value of Metagenomics Next-Generation Sequencing (mNGS) in Detection of Mucormycosis after Chemotherapy in Children with Acute Leukemia. Evidence-based Complementary and Alternative Medicine, 2022.

population.population_description: Children with acute leukemia who developed mucormycosis after chemotherapy, diagnosed by mNGS; all were in agranulocytosis state during infection

neutropenic_status: All 7 in agranulocytosis; duration 45 days in the AML case, 8-18 days in ALL cases
reference_standard: mNGS itself was the diagnostic basis in all 7 patients; one case confirmed by postoperative pathology (hexamine silver staining of resected lung lobe); conventional tests (blood/sputum culture, fungal smear, GM, G) were negative in all

diagnostic_yield.basis: 7/7 patients mNGS-positive for Mucorales (Rhizopus microsporus, R. delemar, Rhizomucor pusillus, Cunninghamella bertholletiae); no denominator of tested-suspected patients - all enrolled were mNGS-positive

additional_yield_vs_conventional: All conventional microbiological tests (blood culture, sputum culture, sputum fungal smear, GM, G test) negative in all 7 children; only mNGS identified the pathogen in all cases; 1/7 had positive hexamine-silver staining on resected lung
turnaround_time: 1-2 days from specimen submission to mNGS report; time from symptom onset to pathogen diagnosis 2-15 days (mean 7.85 days)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single-center pediatric case series; all patients selected because they were mNGS-positive (incorporation/selection bias)

quadas2_notes: Case series with no comparator cohort and no consecutive sampling of suspected infections; mNGS used as diagnostic criterion (incorporation bias); patient flow diagram (reference 6) not reported; QUADAS-2 risk of bias high in patient selection and reference standard.

evidence_quotes.quote: To retrospectively analyze the clinical data of 7 patients with acute leukemia combined with trichomoniasis after chemotherapy in the department of hematology and oncology of Hebei Children's Hospital
In this study, we retrospectively analyzed seven children with acute leukemia who had early infection detected by the mNGS method after chemotherapy for leukemia from January 2020 to December 2021

There were 6 males and 1 female. ... 6 cases of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and 1 case of acute myeloid leukemia. ... All 7 patients ... were in agranulocytosis state during the course of the disease. The blood culture, sputum culture, sputum fungal smear, galactomannan (GM test) and 1,3 β D glucan (G test) were all negative.

In our study, blood cultures, sputum cultures, fungal smears in sputum, G and GM tests were negative in all children sent for examination. Only one case of resected diseased lung lobe was positive for hexosamine-silver staining
In all cases, it took only 1–2 days from specimen submission to report the test results.
The time from symptom onset to diagnosis of pathogenic bacteria in 7 cases was 2–15 days, with an average of 7.85 days.
After treatment, 1 case died, 2 cases were cured, and 4 cases improved.
In our study, we used the mNGS assay to obtain evidence of pathogenic bacteria by infecting children with PB, BAL, and CSF. Four different mucus genera were identified

exclusion_reason: Small single-arm case series (n=7); all patients enrolled were mNGS-positive (no suspected-infection denominator); no reference standard independent of mNGS; no comparator 2x2 possible.
